source.title: Overfitting in adversarially robust deep learning
source.authors: L. Rice; Eric Wong; J. Kolter

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error over training epochs and model widths, but in adversarially trained networks, a different setting from the general double-descent claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own robust test-error results over epochs and network width. It does not sweep training-sample size. Double-descent findings cited from other work are context, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own robust test error over model width (Wide ResNet width sweep) and over training epochs, in adversarially trained networks. This is a new setting for the model-wise (V1) and epoch-wise (V2) claims.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that robust overfitting over epochs is pervasive in adversarial training. They find that model-wise double descent still occurs, peaking at width 5 well before robust interpolation, with larger width improving both best and final robust error. They argue that double descent fails to explain robust overfitting, and that early stopping matches or beats other remedies.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures test error over training and model width, but applies adversarial training and robust-error evaluation rather than the usual non-adversarial setting; its size sweep varies Wide ResNet width.
record.method_sensitivity: The epoch-wise outcome varies with learning-rate schedule, architecture, dataset, perturbation norm, and training algorithm. The TRADES schedule on pre-activation ResNet18 is the reported exception without clear degradation.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard (clean) test error of adversarially trained models does not rise over epochs; final minus best is negative in most Table 3 settings. Robust error does rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In adversarial training, the epoch-wise rise is specific to robust error, not clean error.

fits_no_version.finding: ℓ1/ℓ2 regularization, cutout and mixup reduce robust overfitting only by over-regularizing. Semi-supervised data removes the rise but adds high variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tuned explicit regularization does not remove the epoch-wise robust-overfitting rise without hurting final robust error.

fits_no_version.finding: At every width, the best checkpoint beats the final model. The authors argue that epoch-wise robust overfitting and model-wise double descent are separate phenomena.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch and width axes act separately on robust test error in adversarial training.

record.problems: The width sweep is presented mainly in figures, without a full numerical table of errors by width. ImageNet uses continued training from released models with incomplete prior-training information for one model, and the authors report substantial variability there. The results concern adversarially robust training, not standard training.

untested.parts: Ordinary (non-adversarial) training; architectures other than WRN-28 on CIFAR-10 ℓ∞; the claim that the peak sits at the interpolation threshold, which is reported to differ here.
Ordinary training and label-noise settings where epoch-wise double descent is usually shown; training horizons beyond 200–500 epochs.
Not tested: no sweep of training-sample count.
Not tested: no non-deep model classes.
Not tested: no effective-complexity measure. The authors argue that epochs and width act separately, which bears on V5 only by argument.
Not tested on the double-descent peak: no label-noise sweep, no multiple peaks, no regularization tuned against the width peak.

missing.what: Standard (clean) test error versus width factor, best and final, for the adversarial width sweep
Per-width epoch learning curves showing robust overfitting at every width, including whether any second epoch-wise descent appears
Standard test error final vs best per setting, mostly negative differences (no epoch-wise rise in clean error)

record.verdict_notes: R6 and R16 are the same experiment. R2 and R3 are only informative as a pair. Table 2's ℓ2 'diff 55.2' is a typo; Table 5 gives 8.8. The V2 verdict is limits_scope, not challenges, because the first descent and the rise appear and only the second descent is missing within the trained horizon. The study's horizon (200–500 epochs) and the adversarial setting differ from the original epoch-wise experiments.

versions.untested_parts: The width sweep is for Wide ResNets on CIFAR-10 in the stated adversarial-training setting; the study does not establish the result for ordinary training or other model classes and datasets.
The study tests epoch-wise behavior in adversarially trained models, not ordinary deep-network training.
No sweep of training-sample count near the interpolation threshold.
The model-size sweep is limited to Wide ResNets; other model classes are not tested.
The study does not test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
The study does not test label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peak.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters.

statements.correction: Default piecewise schedule: 200 epochs; multiple decay: 500 epochs; cyclic schedule: improvement followed by overfitting in each of two phases, best checkpoint near the end of phase two; short TRADES/PreAct ResNet18: no degradation within 100 epochs, not converged; ImageNet: continued pretrained-model training, with unknown prior ℓ∞ schedule.
statements.problem: The stated schedule lengths and short-TRADES exception are supported, but a blanket absence of second descent overlooks the cyclic schedule's two improvement phases. ImageNet results cover continued training rather than a complete known trajectory.
